item.title: Universal Planckian dissipation in the strange metal state of the cuprates
item.description:
📚 Nature Communications
👤 A. Shekhter, B. J. Ramshaw, M. K. Chan, N. Harrison
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75673-7 Through an analysis of existing data, the authors show that the “Planckian” relaxation rate in cuprate superconductors is doping independent. This follows from the finding that the square optical plasma frequency scales linearly with doping, which they further argue is a natural consequence of Mott physics.

item.title: Imaging shallow magma storage and fluid pathways beneath Aso volcano using ambient-noise tomography
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Takeshi Tsuji, Chanmaly Chhun, Rezkia Andajani, Yoshihiko Ishikawa, Naoki Nishizaka, Hiromichi Yano
To investigate the high-resolution three-dimensional internal structure of the large caldera-type volcano Mt. Aso, we deployed a temporary seismometer network and applied ambient-noise surface-wave tomography. We resolve the shallow crustal structure with high spatial resolution and identify an ellipsoidal low S-wave velocity (Vs) anomaly at depths of 2.5–4.5 km beneath the Nakadake crater. The Vs within this zone is ~ 1.5 km/s, indicating a highly fractured and pressurized rock, which we interpret as a shallow magma storage zone. Considering the temperature conditions, supercritical fluids could transition to a gas phase within the storage zone, leading to volume expansion, fracturing opening, and reduced Vs.
